name: Korean
caution: 125,902 of the reference words come from a newspaper corpus (Leipzig Corpora Collection, kor_news_2022_1M, 18.5 million words); 279,117 come from the subtitle list. Written sources are more formal than subtitles and contain more names and foreign words. Frequencies of the corpus-only words come from that corpus and are not comparable with subtitle frequencies. Korean is written in syllable blocks; every block is decomposed into its jamo (initial consonant, vowel, optional final consonant), and the jamo are the letters: length, OLD20, Coltheart's N and the n-gram models count jamo (한 = 3, 안 = 3), as in Korean psycholinguistics. A Syllables column gives the block count. Initial ㅇ is a silent place-holder, so it counts as a letter but not in the CV pattern (안 = VC, 한 = CVC). Compound vowels (ㅘ, ㅢ) and double finals (ㄳ, ㄺ) are single jamo. Only jamo strings that recompose into blocks are kept.

english_contamination_removed.rule: Leipzig-only words of 5+ letters that are English words with Zipf >= 4.5

reference_lexicon: plain words (alphabet only) with Zipf >= 2.0 and corpus count >= 3

model.trigram_variants: plain maximum-likelihood letter trigrams with two start markers and one end marker; type counts (each word once) or token counts (each word weighted by its per-million frequency)

filters.not_a_corpus_form: rejected if it occurs anywhere in the corpus word list
filters.phonotactic_legality: initial, medial and final consonant clusters and vowel sequences must each occur in >= 3 reference words

metrics.old20: mean Levenshtein distance to the 20 closest reference words
metrics.logprob: mean log2 probability per letter (incl. word end); model = generating model, all = all-words model

generation.target_rule: per generator and training set: number of training words, between 5000 and 40000

bible_skipped.reason: large corpus; Bible texts are used for small-corpus languages only

realword_filter.rule: a bank item is dropped if a Hunspell dictionary (affixes on, compounding off, lower-case or capitalised) accepts it, if it is a UniMorph lemma or form, or if it occurs (in lower case, in cased scripts) in a Bible translation
